Thanks for the flag, Chloe. Quick assessment below — I've included text we can propose as a tracked redline and guidance on negotiation posture.

1) Liability cap
- Proposal: For this renewal only, Redwood will accept a liability cap equal to 12 months of fees, limited to direct damages. We will add explicit carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and breaches of confidentiality/data protection (i.e., those are uncapped).

Proposed redline snippet (to insert into Section 9):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, for Customer's Renewal effective 2026-10-01 and subject to Customer's execution of the associated Order Form committing to a minimum 36-month term or a 2x committed capacity uplift, Redwood's aggregate liability for direct damages shall not exceed the amount equal to twelve (12) months of fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form. The foregoing limitation shall not apply to liability arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of Customer's data protection obligations."

2) Audit logs & retention
- Ops note: Naomi, 7 years is unusual but feasible if we surface as an add-on export service — recommend we offer automated monthly exports (CSV) plus secure archive for a 3rd-party retention period; cost to customer: $Xk/year (we need ops to confirm X).

3) SLA changes
- Keep uptime definition as-is but accept credit cadence change to automatic credits applied within 30 days for sustained outages > X hours. We should avoid changing core uptime calc.

Next steps
- Chloe / Ben: propose we send them a tracked redline that (a) accepts 12 months tied to 36-mo / uplift, (b) offers audit logs as paid add-on and (c) accepts the credit cadence change. If they insist on 12 months for a 24-mo term, we should push back.
- I'll draft the tracked MSA response today and include the proposed language; Ben, can you confirm commercial flexibility on the term/price trade?
